system/boot_logos/boot_logo_enix_palette.blockNote:
Enix logo palette thinker for OBJ palette 0 (Bank 00, 47167-47186). The palette cycle of the Enix logo is run by three thinkers, one per OBJ palette: this one (OBJ palette 0, CGRAM colours $81-$8F, bundles $50 / $52 / $54), boot_logo_enix_palette_obj1 (OBJ palette 1, $91-$9F, bundles $51 / $53 / $55) and boot_logo_enix_palette_obj2 (OBJ palette 2, $A1-$AF, bundles $56 / $57 / $58). Scene $FB's thinker list (thinker_spawn_0CEB1D, slot 0, param #01) spawns all three together. They start with the scene and run side by side, in BOTH visits of scene $FB (sFB_boot_logo reloads the scene for the second logo), so each visit animates OBJ palettes 0, 1 and 2 at once. Only the second logo, the Enix logo (sprite_group_000010 in spm_boot_logos), uses those palettes, so only it changes colour; the first logo is on OBJ palette 3, which no thinker touches, so in the first visit these thinkers run unseen.

This thinker plays palette bundles $50, $52 and $54 in order: PaletteStart selects a bundle and PaletteStep runs it to its end (the op continues only when the bundle is finished), three times, then KillThinker. The param byte #01 is never read (PaletteStart overwrites animScratch+2 with the bundle ID). Header word $0800: bit 11 keeps it running in the lighter frame routines, bit 2 is clear (runs before the actors).

=== THE BUNDLES (palette_bundles, bank $16) ===

Each bundle has 8 sub-entries of one frame each. A frame is 15 colors (30 bytes) written to CGRAM colors $81 to $8F, i.e. colors 1 to 15 of OBJ palette 0 (boot_logo_enix_palette_obj1 writes $91 to $9F, OBJ palette 1, and boot_logo_enix_palette_obj2 $A1 to $AF, OBJ palette 2). There is 1 extra tick between frames in $50 and $52 and 3 in $54.
$50 (palette_bundle_enix_obj0_reveal): starts all black; a 13-color ramp from dark purple ($2C4B) to white ($7FFF) grows across colors 1 to 13, its white tip moving from color 1 to color 13 with the darker colors trailing it; colors 14 and 15 stay 0.
$52 (palette_bundle_enix_obj0_whiten): the ramp turns white from its bright end towards its dark end until all 13 colors are white, while colors 14 and 15 brighten from $18C6 / $2108 to $4E73 / $6739.
$54 (palette_bundle_enix_obj0_settle): starts all white and fades back down to the ramp (steps through $777D, $6AFA, ... to $2C4B ... $7FFF) while colors 14 and 15 darken to $1425 / $2449.
So the logo's palette sweeps in, flashes to white and settles on a rainbow ramp: a shine effect. This is read from the colour values (not run).

=== WHERE THE COLOURS LAND ===

In sprite_group_000010 (the second logo, spm_boot_logos) OBJ palette 0 colours 8 of the 16 parts of the 4 x 4 emblem block (parts $05 to $0A, $0E, $0F: the lower two rows), OBJ palette 1 the other 8 (parts $00 to $04, $0B to $0D: the upper two rows). Both get the same shine at the same time, so the emblem sweeps in, flashes white and settles.

=== CORRECTIONS ===

The three thinkers were first called boot_logo_palette_enix, boot_logo_palette_quintet and boot_logo_palette_third. Those were spawn-order names and read like three companies or three steps; they are one palette cycle, the Enix logo's, split over OBJ palettes 0, 1 and 2 (the old header's 'animates the Enix logo colors' was right for all three). The old header called this the first of three thinkers and the Quintet note said it runs 'after the Enix palette sequence'; they are spawned together and run in parallel. The logo is the second logo of scene $FB, the 4 x 4 emblem with a wordmark under it; I054 left the question of which logo uses OBJ palettes 0 and 1 open (OQ-I054-1) and the sprite tables answer it.

partNotes.boot_logo_enix_palette_obj0: Thinker, part 1 of the Enix logo palette cycle: bundles $50, $52 and $54 on OBJ palette 0 (CGRAM colors $81 to $8F): reveal, flash to white, settle.

system/boot_logos/boot_logo_enix_palette.blockNote:
Enix logo palette thinker for OBJ palette 1 (Bank 00, 47187-47206): the second of the three thinkers that run the Enix logo's palette cycle (see boot_logo_enix_palette_obj0). Spawned together with it and boot_logo_enix_palette_obj2 by scene $FB's thinker list (thinker_spawn_0CEB1D, slot 1, param #02, never read) and run in parallel with them in both visits of the scene.

Plays palette bundles $51, $53 and $55 in order (PaletteStart + PaletteStep each), then KillThinker. The bundles (palette_bundle_enix_obj1_reveal / _whiten / _settle) hold exactly the same colour frames as $50, $52 and $54 (see boot_logo_enix_palette_obj0) but write them to CGRAM colors $91 to $9F, colors 1 to 15 of OBJ palette 1, with the same 1 / 1 / 3 extra ticks. So the effect is a black to rainbow-ramp reveal, a white flash and a settle.
OBJ palette 1 colours 8 of the 16 parts of the 4 x 4 emblem block of the second logo (parts $00 to $04 and $0B to $0D of sprite_group_000010: the upper two rows); boot_logo_enix_palette_obj0 does the other 8 with palette 0. The first logo does not use it.

=== CORRECTIONS ===

The old name was boot_logo_palette_quintet, a spawn-order name that read like a second company; this is the same Enix logo as the other two thinkers, on OBJ palette 1. The old header said it runs 'after the Enix palette sequence'; it runs at the same time. The I054 note gave the spawn param as #01; the three slots carry #01, #02 and #03 and this one is #02 (none is read). Which logo uses OBJ palette 1 (OQ-I054-1) is answered by the sprite tables: the second logo's emblem, the Enix logo.

partNotes.boot_logo_enix_palette_obj1: Thinker, part 2 of the Enix logo palette cycle: bundles $51, $53 and $55 on OBJ palette 1 (CGRAM colors $91 to $9F): the same reveal, flash and settle as boot_logo_enix_palette_obj0.

system/boot_logos/boot_logo_enix_palette.blockNote:
Enix logo palette thinker for OBJ palette 2 (Bank 00, 47207-47226): the third of the three thinkers that run the Enix logo's palette cycle, the one for the block under the emblem. Scene $FB's thinker list (thinker_spawn_0CEB1D, slot 2, param #03, never read) spawns it together with boot_logo_enix_palette_obj0 and boot_logo_enix_palette_obj1. All three run side by side in BOTH visits of the scene (sFB_boot_logo reloads the scene for the second logo).

It plays palette bundles $56, $57 and $58 in order (PaletteStart selects a bundle, PaletteStep runs it to its end), then KillThinker. The bundles write CGRAM colors $A1 to $AF, colors 1 to 15 of OBJ palette 2 (30 bytes per frame, 8 frames per bundle, 1 extra tick per frame, 33 on the last frame of $58).
$56 (palette_bundle_enix_obj2_fill_a): starts black and fills the 15 colors with the flat purple $68DA one at a time (colors 1 to 8 over the 8 frames).
$57 (palette_bundle_enix_obj2_fill_b): continues the fill from 9 colors to all 15 (the last two frames are both full).
$58 (palette_bundle_enix_obj2_dip): starts all purple; a darker dip opens around color 7 and gets wider and deeper each frame, ending in a V-shaped ramp from $64B9 at the ends down to $3C4F in the middle (colors 14 and 15 stay $68DA / $70DC), which is held for 34 ticks.
This is read from the colour values (not run).

=== WHERE THE COLOURS LAND ===

OBJ palette 2 is used only by the 4 x 2 block of 16 x 16 parts under the emblem in sprite_group_000010 (parts $10 to $17 of the second logo, see spm_boot_logos). The first logo is on OBJ palette 3, which no thinker touches, so in the first visit this thinker runs unseen.

=== CORRECTIONS ===

The old name was boot_logo_palette_third (the third spawn slot). The old header called this the 'third and final logo palette thinker' that 'completes the boot logo palette rotation before gameplay begins' and described #56, #57 and #58 as palette animations. It is the third of three parallel thinkers, not a later step, #56 to #58 are palette bundles, and it animates only OBJ palette 2 of the second logo, the Enix logo.

partNotes.boot_logo_enix_palette_obj2: Thinker, part 3 of the Enix logo palette cycle: bundles $56, $57 and $58 on OBJ palette 2 (CGRAM colors $A1 to $AF): a purple fill, then a deepening dip in the middle of the ramp.

system/boot_logos/sFB_boot_logo.asm.blockNote:
Boot logo sequence actor - scene $FB master controller (the first scene of the game). Scene $FB is entered TWICE at power-on and shows one logo per visit; the second logo then hands over to the title screen scene $FC.

=== SEQUENCE ===

1. BootLogoInit (both visits): sets displayModeFlags bit 14 (no reader found, OQ-I034-1), clears colour 0 of the palette staging buffer, enables FastROM (MEMSEL = $01), puts only the sprite layer on the main screen (TM = $10, bit 4 = OBJ; no BG is shown), masks the joypad, then reads STAT78 bit 4: 0 = 60 Hz NTSC continues, 1 = 50 Hz PAL jumps to BootLogoPalLockout.
2. First visit (event flag $10 clear): nudge the actor Y -16, play sprite animation #01 (sprite_group_000112, a 96 x 48 logo on OBJ palette 3) for 2 passes of 60 ticks = 120 ticks, set event flag $10, QueueMapChange to scene $FB itself, Die.
3. Second visit (flag set): BootLogoSecondPhase plays animation #00 (sprite_group_000010, the Enix logo: an emblem with a wordmark under it, OBJ palettes 0, 1, 2 and 4) for 120 ticks, clears flag $10 and queues scene $FC (title screen), Die.
Event flag $10 is not one of the flags the scene load zeroes (only $00 to $0F are), which is why it survives the reload; it is cleared again at the end because the South Cape church scripts (sc08_*) use the same flag.

The three boot_logo_enix_palette_obj* thinkers are spawned by the scene's thinker list in both visits and run the Enix logo's palette cycle on OBJ palettes 0, 1 and 2, i.e. only the second logo (see boot_logo_enix_palette_obj0).

=== PAL LOCKOUT ===

A 50 Hz console never sees a logo: BootLogoPalLockout draws the region warning text (consolestring_01D9D8) on BG3 and then yields forever at SetEntryHere + RTL. The game cannot be started on a PAL console.

=== POSITION ===

The scene's actor-spawn places the actor at tile (7, 8) and InitActorFromSceneData adds 8 pixels of X for normal actors; the first NudgePosition adds another 8, so the actor ends at X = 128, the centre of the 256-pixel screen. The sprite groups are laid out around that origin. QueueMapChange's last operand $1100 is the packed camera-bounds override (InitCameraBounds).

=== SPRITES (spm_boot_logos.sprite.asm) ===

The scene's spritemap card loads spm_boot_logos ($018F bytes) to $7E4000; its two entries are the animation indexes of StageSpriteLoop: #00 = sprite_set_000004 (second logo), #01 = sprite_set_00000A (first logo). Each sprite-set is one frame record (hold $003B = 60 ticks per pass, group pointer) closed by the hidden $FFFF delimiter.
First logo, sprite_group_000112: 96 x 48 px, 16 parts of 16 x 16 in rows of 6, 6 and 4, all OBJ palette 3.
Second logo, sprite_group_000010: 122 x 156 px, 35 parts: a 4 x 4 block (64 x 64) on OBJ palette 1 (upper two rows) and 0 (lower two rows), a 4 x 2 block below it on palette 2, and a row of 11 parts 12 px apart on palette 4. Palettes 0 to 2 are the ones the boot_logo_enix_palette_obj* thinkers animate; palette 4 is static.
Sprite-part = 7 bytes: size flag, X offset and mirrored X, Y offset and mirrored Y, OAM tile word (high byte vhppPPPN, PPP = OBJ palette). Sprite-group = 12 header bytes (X extents left / right, Y extents above / below, 8 bytes nothing reads, identical in both groups), the part count, then the parts. The palettes come from pal_boot_logos (80 colours, OBJ palettes 0 to 4, loaded at CGRAM colour 128). The second logo is the Enix logo (its palette cycle is the three boot_logo_enix_palette_obj* thinkers); which company the first logo belongs to was not checked against the tile art.

=== NOTES ===

The joypad mask in the ROM is $FFFC (db-us/transforms.json rewrites $FFF0 to $FFFC for this block), which hides every pad bit including Start and Select, so no logo can be skipped. The old header said TM = $10 puts BG1 on the main screen and that the mask is $FFF0; TM bit 4 is the OBJ layer and the shipped mask is $FFFC.

actors/layer1_scroll_actors.asm.blockNote:
Layer-1 scroll drivers (Bank 00, 59610-60053): three actor scripts that set the scroll position of the second background layer (cameraDeltaX / Y). They were first grouped as visual_effect_pipeline, a name that suggested sprites or visual effects; they have nothing to do with either.

=== SPAWN ===

- Layer1DriftWrapped: scene actor record < X byte $01, Y byte $82 > in scene_actors entries $09 and $32 (scene_event_0C84BC, scene_event_0C9572).
- Layer1DriftUnbounded: record < $02, $02 > in scene_actors entries $4E and $50 (scene_event_0C9E92, scene_event_0CA01A).
- Layer1ParallaxRatio: sg55_viper_arena (SpawnBeforeFlags #$2800, then $14 := $0201 and $16 := 0) and sg55_mystic_statue code_0ACE81 ($14 := $0201, $16 := $000C).

=== SPAWN BYTES = VELOCITY (the first two actors) ===

InitActorFromSceneData turns the record's X and Y bytes into pixels (byte x 16), so $14 >> 4 gives the X byte back and $16 >> 4 the Y byte. Both are decoded as sign-magnitude: bit 7 = negative, bits 0-6 = magnitude. The Y byte is decremented first, so Y byte 1 = 0, 2 = +1, $82 = -1; Y byte 0 gives $0081 (+129), a quirk the shipped records never use. Result: Layer1DriftWrapped drifts at X +1, Y -1 px per frame; Layer1DriftUnbounded at X +2, Y +1.

=== VARIABLES ===

cameraTargetX / Y ($06BE / $06C2): layer-0 scroll target (camera_scroll_controller). cameraDeltaX / Y ($06C0 / $06C4): the layer-1 scroll POSITION, not a delta: CameraSmoothScroll (camera_tilemap) copies them to effectScrollH / V ($068C / $0690, the BG2 scroll) when layerPriorityFlag bit $0400 is set. effectDeltaX / Y ($06E4 / $06E6): written by camera_scroll_controller, how far the camera moved (target - current scroll); the drifters add it so layer 1 follows the camera. effectBoundsX / Y ($0694 / $0698): layer-1 width and height (set in scene_script). effectRenderDeltaX / Y ($06E8 / $06EA): written only by these actors; no reader was found outside scene_lifecycle, which clears them. forcedScrollOverride ($06C8): written here with bit 15 set, the same convention as ScrollCameraInit; no reader found (OQ-I051-2).

The old header said the actors seed and integrate velocities for 'cutscene camera takeover' and that Layer1ParallaxRatio refines the other two every frame. The velocity decode and the integration are in the same actor, and Layer1ParallaxRatio is independent: its $14 / $16 are a parallax ratio or a drift, not a subpixel remainder.

actors/player_transition_handlers.asm.blockNote:
Player-actor transition scripts plus one impact effect (Bank 00, 50200-50671). Most routines are not run by an actor of their own: a caller (scene script, item code, warp code) writes a routine's address into the player actor's entry pointer ($0000,Y low word and $0002,Y bank byte), clears the player's wait counter ($0008,Y), and the player actor runs the routine on its next turn (X = D = the player slot, so every COP inside acts on the player). The routines hold a pose, play a short sequence or give control back; most finish with JML player_character.PlayerIdleEntry, which also clears playerFlags $2800, so the $0800 script lock set by the caller or the routine is released there.

=== ENTRY POINTS AND CALLERS (from the pointer writes) ===

- SpawnImpactSparkAndDie (50200, the first entry of this file): SpawnListAppend ImpactSparkEffect, then Die. It is the default script written into an actor hit by the player's interaction / push strike (combat_collision.ApplyHitDamageToVictim path 1, together with $10 |= $0040) and is reached by JumpFar from gw8A_sand_fanger (756178).
- ImpactSparkEffect (50211): effect actor: SFX $09, frame $2A of spriteset_enemies, then Die. Spawned by SpawnImpactSparkAndDie and by gw82_archer (SpawnListAppend at X +- 14, Y - 14, flags $0302), so it is an impact spark; it reveals no item (it was first called PlayerItemRevealSpawn; OQ-I052-9).
- PlayerIdleAnimLoop (50226): idle animation loop. Callers: warps_interaction (while the music upload finishes) and ir29_castoth func_0AA37B.
- PlayerStaticBodyPose / PlayerWalkingIdlePose (50246 / 50261): the flute playback in item_use_system holds body 4 frame $1F, then restores control.
- RestorePlayerControlDirect (50266): JML PlayerIdleEntry. Callers: warps_interaction and ir29_castoth func_0AA391.
- PlayerPoseHold / PlayerPoseHoldExit (50270 / 50285): hold body 4 frame $20 (every frame / once, then PlayerIdleEntry). Idle: gs2D_lily, gs2E_sleep, dc2F_adrift, dc31_rescuer. Exit: dc31_kara. They were first called PlayerFreedanRevealIdle / PlayerFreedanRevealExit; the callers do not identify the character as Freedan, so the pose names are neutral (OQ-I052-2).
- PlayerIdleEntryJump (50281): a bare JML PlayerIdleEntry; no reference found.
- PlayerFallFromHeight (50297): awBD_fall_trigger. PlayerSkyGardenJumpLanding (50385): sg4D_jump_handler. PlayerAuraTransformEntry (50519): item_use_system.UseItem_Aura (Shadow only, standing still).

=== FLAG BITS USED ===

Player actor flags $10: $0008 = normal collision-aware movement (cleared while a script moves the player, set again at the end), $0200 = scripted motion marker (the Psycho Slider and the lunge set it too), $2000 = SortActorsByDepth skips the actor and PlayerIdleEntry yields without acting (meaning open: OQ-I025-2), $0040 = death flag. playerFlags $0800 = script / ability lock. layerPriorityFlag ($06EE) bit $0200 = camera frozen (the old comment called it 'force layer priority'). joypadMaskStd |= $CFFC hides every button except Select / Start (the old comment said $CFF0).

The old header's 'item reveal with metasprite staging' is the ImpactSparkEffect spark.

partNotes.ApplyHitDamageToVictim:
Resolve one phase-2 overlap: apply player-strength damage to the overlapped actor (X = victim, $08 = box owner / hitter). It reduces the victim actor's HP; contact damage to the player is ApplyInteractionDamage.

Two main paths based on $24 flag (set by the friendly/interaction detection in the outer loop):

Path 1 ($24 nonzero — interaction/push hit): Checks the enemy's scratch1010+6 ($7F1016,X) for a custom interaction handler. If present, overwrites the enemy's entry point. Otherwise, sets the enemy to SpawnImpactSparkAndDie (player_transition_handlers), marks $0040 (death flag), and dispatches knockback velocity by player facing direction (±4 to extVelocityX/Y).

Path 2 ($24 zero — combat damage, the code under ApplyHitDamageToVictim_DamagePath): Checks if the victim has $0010 in flags10 (invincible) → routes to HitInvincibleVictim. Otherwise computes damage:
  totalStr = playerStr + bonus ($09E2, 0 for hitter slot $1000) + climbStateData
  rawDamage = max(1, totalStr − victimStats[2])   (stats[2] = DEF)
  netDamage = rawDamage + characterForm
Subtracts from enemy HP, spawns damage digits (priority $2B00 with $1000 in spawned actor's $12), handles death (onDeathCallback or StandardEnemyDefeatHandler), and spawns HitStaggerMain for knockback.

After damage: checks and dispatches onHitCallback ($7F1000,X). Assigns iframes ($0011 or $FFEF). Updates HUD HP display. Finally checks extendedFlags $0050 for collision callback processing — clears $FFAF bits, toggles $6000 in $12, and dispatches onCollideCallback.

actors/smooth_follow_child.asm.blockNote:
Straight-line projectile mover (Bank 00, 58587-58964), shared by six enemy projectile scripts. smooth_follow_child is the visible projectile body; a hidden child (SmoothFollowChildTick) aims ONCE at a target actor and then moves along that fixed heading at a fixed speed, copying its position to the body every frame. It does not chase: after the first frame the target is ignored.

=== CALLERS ===

pyCC_blaster (two projectile actors), awB1_wall_walker (code_0BBD19), ec0C_ribber (code_0A843E) and the unused unused_follow_chain set $24 = playerActor, a speed in loopCounter ($7F0014: 1 in pyCC_blaster and ec0C_ribber, 2 in awB1 and gw8A) and then enter smooth_follow_child by a tail call (push of bank and entry minus 1, RTL). gw8A_sand_fanger (code_0B8979) and pyDD_mummy_queen (code_0BA782) skip the body and spawn SmoothFollowChildTick themselves with SpawnAfterMarked (flags $2000), storing playerActor in the child's $24; pyDD uses the speed 4 + $0B02. In every case the spawner is the projectile itself, so the tick moves the spawner.
combat_collision uses SmoothFollowChildDie as the default onCollideCallback: an actor with extendedFlags $0010 and no callback of its own is pointed at it when it touches the player, so these projectiles die after the hit is applied.

=== HOW IT WORKS ===

1. smooth_follow_child clears word $2A, spawns the tick as a hidden marked child (flags $2000) and gives it the target in $24. If the pool is full (Y = $1FC0) it dies at once. Then it plays AnimOnce every frame and dies when its own $10 bit $4000 is set. That bit is the off-screen flag SortActorsByDepth sets when the actor box is completely off the screen; it is not set by a parent. Die also kills the marked tick.
2. On its first frame the tick copies the body's loopCounter (the speed: pixels per frame on the dominant axis), forms dx = target.X - self.X and dy = target.Y - 8 - self.Y, stores |dx| in $0018 and |dy| in $001C (global scratch words, not actor fields) and picks one of 8 handlers from the signs and from which magnitude is larger.
3. The handler calls ComputeFollowAngle (Y-dominant) or ComputeFollowAngleAlt (X-dominant) once. That fills orbitAngle with a slope row of smooth_follow's dither table and clears the dither phase. COP SetEntryHere then saves the address of the next instruction, so every later frame resumes AFTER the aim: ComputeFollowStep gives $0000 = major-axis pixels (loopCounter) and $0002 = minor-axis pixels (0 or 1 per pixel from the slope row), the handler applies them to the tick's own X/Y with its fixed signs, and SmoothFollowWriteParentPos copies X/Y to the body (the tick's $04 prev-link). The heading never changes.

=== HANDLER HEADINGS ===

dx >= 0, dy >= 0 (target south-east): |dy| >= |dx| SmoothFollowApplySSE (Y += major, X += minor); |dy| < |dx| SmoothFollowApplyESE (X += major, Y += minor).
dx >= 0, dy < 0 (north-east): |dy| >= |dx| SmoothFollowApplyNNE (Y -= major, X += minor); |dy| < |dx| SmoothFollowApplyENE (X += major, Y -= minor).
dx < 0, dy >= 0 (south-west): |dy| >= |dx| SmoothFollowApplySSW (Y += major, X -= minor); |dy| < |dx| SmoothFollowApplyWSW (X -= major, Y += minor).
dx < 0, dy < 0 (north-west): |dy| >= |dx| SmoothFollowApplyNNW (Y -= major, X -= minor); |dy| < |dx| SmoothFollowApplyWNW (X -= major, Y -= minor).
Each handler is named after the heading it fires. Five of them were first called SmoothFollowApplyEastPrimary (SSE), EastSecondary (SSW), WestPrimary (WSW), WestSecondary (WNW) and SouthPrimary (NNW), which described neither the dominant axis nor the direction, and three (NNE, ENE, ESE) had only loc_ labels.

=== CORRECTIONS ===

The old header said the actor makes a child 'smoothly chase a reference actor', that it updates 'both actors' positions each frame' and that it dies 'when the parent actor sets flag $4000 or on special actor ID $1FC0'. The aim is taken once; only the tick moves and it writes the body's position; $4000 is the body's own off-screen flag and $1FC0 is the pool-exhausted result of the spawn.

partNotes.SmoothFollowApplySSE: Heading SSE: target south-east (dx >= 0, dy >= 0) with |dy| >= |dx|. ComputeFollowAngle once, then each frame Y += major ($0000) and X += minor ($0002).
partNotes.SmoothFollowApplySSW: Heading SSW: target south-west (dx < 0, dy >= 0) with |dy| >= |dx|. ComputeFollowAngle once, then each frame Y += major and X -= minor. Reached from the west half of the tick.
partNotes.SmoothFollowApplyNNW: Heading NNW: target north-west with |dy| >= |dx|. ComputeFollowAngle once, then each frame Y -= major and X -= minor.

functions/EnemyDropSystem.asm.blockNote:
Enemy drop spawner for gems and heals (Bank 00, 57129-57340). The old names (DarkGemDropSystem, SpawnDarkGemType1 and so on) said 'dark gem', but what drops is a pickup carrying item id $83 to $86 of GiveItemToPlayer: 1, 2 or 5 gems, or a 5 HP heal.

=== CALLER ===

StandardEnemyDefeatHandler reaches EnemyGemDropRouter when the defeated enemy's stat byte +3 (enemy-stats gemDropType) is nonzero and either this scene's reward flag $0300 is set or enemies remain (the last enemy of a scene whose reward is still unclaimed gets the stat reward instead of a gem). The router spawns one of three entries with SpawnListAppend (flags $0420, so the pickup inherits the dead enemy's position through CopyActorState): value 1 = SpawnDropGem1 (fixed $83), value 2 = SpawnDropGem2 (fixed $84), any other nonzero value (3) = SpawnDropByHpTier (random, see below).

=== THE PICKUP ===

The actor carries its item id in chatPtr ($7F000A,X) and has the 'friendly' flag $0020 in its $10 (from the spawn flags). When the player overlaps it, combat_collision.InteractionDamage_NPCChat calls GiveItemToPlayer(chatPtr) and turns the actor into NpcDespawnStub. Ids: $83 = 1 gem, $84 = 2 gems, $85 = 5 gems (cap 999), $86 = hpToHeal += 5 (UpdateHUD refills 1 HP every 8 frames) plus the spark effect and SFX $22.
Each entry also spawns a marked child, interaction_handlers.collect_handler_gem (flags $2700), which pulls the pickup toward the player while L / R is held. The pickup is the marked parent ($12 bit $0040 set by SpawnAfterMarked), so its Die also removes the child. Each body clears $10 bit $0400 that the $0420 spawn flags set (see OQ-I049-3).

=== LIFETIME (spriteset_enemies animation lists) ===

Gems: anim 4 / 5 / 6 (gems $83 / $84 / $85) for 10 passes (about 75 ticks each: a 60-tick still frame and 5 shimmer frames of 3 ticks, about 750 ticks), then the blink anim 9 / $0A / $0B for 150 passes (2 ticks each, about 300 ticks), then Die. Heal: anim $22 for 180 passes (2 ticks, about 360 ticks), then anim $35 for 60 passes (4 ticks, about 240 ticks), then Die.

=== WEIGHTED DROP (SpawnDropByHpTier) ===

HP tier by the player's HP against max HP: HP <= max/4 uses table group $20, HP <= max/2 uses group $10, otherwise group 0. A random byte is compared against the group's four ascending thresholds (the last is $0100, so it always matches) and the first row whose threshold is above the byte gives the body to run. Probabilities of 256 outcomes:
HP above half: $86 heal 5.9%, $85 5 gems 17.6%, $84 2 gems 36.3%, $83 1 gem 40.2%. HP between a quarter and a half: $85 9.8%, $83 19.9%, $86 30.1%, $84 40.2%. HP at or below a quarter: $84 4.7%, $83 15.2%, $85 29.7%, $86 50.4%. The heal becomes the likeliest drop when the player is low on HP.

functions/StandardEnemyDefeatHandler.asm.blockNote:
Standard field-enemy defeat script (Bank 00, 56202-56816). The defeated actor itself runs it (X = D = the victim). Entered in three ways: (1) as the default death script: hit_stagger_controller (HitStaggerResolveHit) and two inline paths in combat_collision set the victim's entry point to StandardEnemyDefeatHandler when its HP reaches zero and it has no onDeathCallback ($7F1004); (2) by COP JumpFar from the own scripts of 13 enemies (pyCC_mystic_ball, pyD2_haunt, awB1_wall_walker, pyDD_mummy_queen, gw83_asp, mu67_vampires, av6E_draco, sg55_viper, sg4D_dynapede, sg4E_nitropede, sg4D_cyber, ir29_castoth, sg51_statue) and from EnemyDefeatDispatch (the last enemy of a scene); (3) ir20_statue and ir26_statue JumpFar straight into EnemyDefeatFlashAndDrop.

=== FLOW ===

1. Kill counters (StandardEnemyDefeatHandler). Skipped when statsPtr points at the first enemy_stats_table entry (an EnemyInitBasic actor: HP 1, no stats) or extendedFlags bit $0080 (the boss bit). Otherwise enemiesRemainingBcd ($0AEE) -= 1 in decimal mode, enemiesRemaining ($0AEC) -= 1 in hex, and the new count is also kept in orbitAngle ($7F0010,X): 0 means this was the last enemy on the map.
2. Flash (EnemyDefeatFlashAndDrop). Movement is halted ($2C / $2E and moveScratch1 / 2 := 0), SFX #06 plays on channel 1 and EnemyDeathFlash is spawned at the enemy (flags $0302; bit $0002 draws it in front of every actor). The flash gets $12 bit $1000 (CopyActorState clears it) so that it keeps running in display-filter actor mode, then WaitByte 2.
3. No-stats and boss actors go to EnemyDefeatBossCleanup: hide ($10 |= $2000), ClearSolidHere if extendedFlags $0008, WaitByte 5, Die. They get no kill flag, gem drop or reward.
4. Other enemies: SetDungeonKillFlag (the enemyNum bit in wramFlags, so the enemy stays dead on re-entry), then the gem decision, hide ($10 |= $2000), ClearSolidHere if extendedFlags $0008, the field reveal, and finally Die when enemies remain or EnemyStatBonusReward when this was the last one.
   Gem decision: TestFlag_0300 (event flag $0300 + scene = this scene's clear reward was already claimed) set, or orbitAngle nonzero (enemies remain): drop a gem when the stats byte +3 (gemDropType) is nonzero, through EnemyGemDropRouter. Last enemy with the reward still unclaimed: no gem, the stat reward replaces it.
   Field reveal: deathActionIdx ($7F0024,X) nonzero and event flag $0100 + idx still clear: set it and spawn SpawnFieldRevealEffect (flags $0342, with $12 $1000), handing it the index.
5. EnemyStatBonusReward (last enemy only): enemy_clear_reward_table[scene] selects the pickup (0 none, 1 HP, 2 STR, 3 or more DEF) unless the scene flag $0300 is already set. It sets displayModeFlags $0080 (display-filter actor mode: only actors with $12 $1000 run, so the world freezes while the pickup plays), spawns reward_actors.e_hp_increase / e_str_increase / e_def_increase (flags $1000, $12 $1000) and Dies. RewardActorVFX sets the scene flag later (see reward_actors).

=== CORRECTIONS ===

The old header said ComposeDigitSprites_AtCursor assigns this as the OnDeath callback during enemy setup (no code there references it; the engine falls back to it when $7F1004 is empty), that it is about 360 bytes (it spans about 614), that it calls ClearLowHere (the COP is ClearSolidHere) and that the $12 $1000 write is a 'priority boost'. The comment on the first block said the gem drop is skipped when scene flag $0300 is set; it is the opposite: gems drop when the flag is set or enemies remain. EnemyDropSystem.asm repeated the inverted condition (corrected there). The 'about 20 enemy actor scripts' were 13 JumpFar sites, EnemyDefeatDispatch, 2 statues and 3 engine sites.

system/dark_space/sE6_gaia.asm.blockNote:
Dark Space / Gaia hub (scene $E6, the room reached from the Dark Space portals and from the diary menu's load) plus a shared character-transformation library (Bank 08, 579499-587528; GaiaNpcSprite and GaiaVoiceSparkle in Bank 09, 630928-630997). The same spawn list is also used by scene $09, which has no scene-meta entry. scene_meta_00E6 loads spm_darkspace_sprites ($0579 bytes) and plays track $16 (bgm_space_beyond_time).

=== STRUCTURE ===

DarkSpaceMainInit spawns three children with SpawnAfter: FireflySpawnerLoop, GaiaNpcSprite and GaiaVoiceSparkle. SpawnAfter inserts each new actor right after the parent, so the main actor's $06 link ends up on the LAST one spawned, the voice sparkle (the old notes called it the Gaia NPC link). Every 'LDY $06 / STA $0024, Y' below is therefore the voice sparkle's on / off switch ($FFFF = on, 0 = off), not an NPC interaction lock.
It then validates globalScriptIndex ($0AAC: the room variant, written by the portal actor or restored by the diary load; 4 or more becomes 0), keeps it in $0AB2 (saved with the game, restored by the diary menu), clears $0AAC and switch-cases to a layout: 0 DS_LayoutBasic (Gaia only), 1 DS_LayoutTransform (statues chosen by characterForm), 2 DS_LayoutAbility (ability orb chosen by the scene), 3 DS_LayoutSpecial (sets $0AAC = 1 and runs layout 1; this is the pyramid's Dark Space, where GaiaHint_AuraItem tests $0AAC and gives the Aura item).
Every room polls BranchIfPlayerInAbsTiles zones (x1, y1, x2, y2 in tiles): Gaia (7,8)-(9,9) = GaiaDialogueEntry, left statue (3,A)-(5,B), right statue (B,A)-(D,B), exit (5,D)-(B,F) = DarkSpaceExit. Each room has a wait state (the player is still standing in a zone: nothing happens, so a dialogue cannot retrigger) and an active state that dispatches the zones; the *Wait / *TileWait pairs and the loc_ labels after them are these two states.
The called scripts (GaiaDialogueEntry, the *TransformDialogue routines) are entered with CallNear and end with RestoreSavedPtr, which returns to the room loop.

=== EXIT ===

DarkSpaceExit masks the joypad, hides the player ($10 |= $2000), puts this actor on him, plays SFX $0C on both channels and the dissolve animation $1C of spriteset_enemies once, waits 30 ticks (WaitByte #1D), then fills the warp words: sceneNext = $0B12 (the scene the player warped from, saved by ExecuteWarp), player spawn X = $0B08 x 16 and Y = ($0B0C + 2) x 16 (the source warp rectangle's tile position), facing 3 and the packed camera window $0B10 / $0B11 -> warpScrollParams. gfxCacheIdxB = $0101 is the transition speed (exit and enter 1), gfxCacheIdxA = $0002 is exit effect 2 = mosaic, enter effect 0 = fade. The old notes called the destination a camera position and $0101 a brightness fade.

=== GAIA DIALOGUE ===

GaiaDialogueEntry: 6-tick pause (WaitByte #05), voice sparkle on, first visit (event flag $DC) the intro text, then GaiaHealAndHints. If HP < max it prints the 'hurt' text and writes hpToHeal = 40; UpdateHUD turns that request into +1 HP every 8 frames (SFX $0D) until HP = max (the loop yields until then). The hint is chosen by the position of the source scene in GaiaHintSceneTable (34 scenes, one GaiaHint_xx handler each; 21 of them have no text and go straight to the save prompt). GaiaSavePrompt: 'Record what's happened so far?' (DialogueOptions: entry 0 = cancel, 1 = first option, 2 = second option). Record = SaveGameState_Scene for the active slot ($0D8C), SFX $29, 60 ticks (WaitByte #3B), then 'Continue your journey?': Yes (entry 1) = GaiaThenGo, 'Then go.', returns to the room; No (entry 2) = GaiaThenRest, 'Then rest a while.', fades to track $0E (bgm_longing_for_the_past) and the actor yields forever. GaiaThenGo and GaiaThenRest are named after the answers 'Then go.' and 'Then rest a while.'; each is reached from two prompts (they were first called GaiaDontRecord and GaiaContinueJourney after the first prompt only, which made them look swapped for the second).

=== FORMS AND ABILITIES ===

characterForm ($0AD4): 0 Will, 1 Freedan, 2 Shadow. A statue dialogue writes a Transform_* routine into the player actor's entry pointer ($0000 / $0002, $0008 = 0) and sets playerFlags $0800; the player then plays it (player body entry #05, the transformation frames), the routine sets characterForm and DarkSpaceRestoreControl clears $0800 and sends the player back to PlayerIdleEntry. The Shadow statue needs event flag $B4, whose only writer is daC8_neil (the Neil reunion in the Dao dormitory; the old header said it is unlocked at Ankor Wat); first Freedan visit flag $F7, first Shadow visit flag $DD.
The Transform_* routines are a shared library: Transform_WillToShadow is entered from sE5_epilogue, pyDD_mummy_queen, gw8A_sand_fanger, mu67_vampires, sg55_viper, ir29_castoth and btE4_kara; Transform_ShadowToWill from pyDD_mummy_queen, gw8A_sand_fanger, mu67_vampires, sg55_viper, ir29_castoth and pyCD_jackal; Transform_FreedanToWill from sg55_mystic_statue, ir29_transform, ir1C_lily, ec13_lily, pyCD_jackal and mu67_bomb (13 files in all).
AbilitySceneTable has 6 entries of (scene, abilityBitmask bit): $15 Psycho Dash $01, $62 Psycho Slider $02, $86 Spin Dash $04, $42 Dark Friar $10, $A7 Aura Barrier $20, $B8 Earthquaker $40, ended by $00. The low nibble holds the Will abilities, the high nibble the Freedan abilities; the old header called byte 1 'ability index + statue type'. The table position is the ability index used by table_08EB8F (names) and table_08EBD3 (descriptions) through globalScriptIndex. DS_LayoutAbility shows the orb for the current scene (BG change $86 and orb at (64,109) for a Will ability, $8B and (64,84) for a Freedan ability); AbilityOrbActor dies when the bit is already in abilityBitmask, otherwise waits for the player at the statue zone, turns him into the form that can use it (Will for the low nibble, Freedan for the high nibble) with LookupAbilityForm, ORs the bit in, plays the orb flight, fanfare (track $18) and the two texts.

=== SPRITES (spm_darkspace_sprites) ===

Animation #00 (4 frames, hold $63 then $0C x 3) is GaiaNpcSprite; #01 to #03 are the three sparkle variants of GaiaVoiceSparkle; #0A (32 frames of hold 0, a 16 x 16 spark alternating with an 8 x 8 tile) is the ability orb. #04 to #09 (8 x 8 effect tiles) are not used by this file. FireflyParticle and DarkSpaceExit use spriteset_enemies.

=== NOT REFERENCED ===

No reference was found in extracted/ for: DS_AuraItemRoom and its handlers, AuraItemInteraction and its helpers (with dialogstring_08EFEF / 08F003 / 08F060), DarkSpaceAmbientParticle, the code at loc_08DA6B / loc_08DA77 (after an unconditional BRA), and the unused hint strings dialogstring_08DEC6, 08E066, 08E0C7, 08E109, 08E19C, 08E261, 08E2B9 and 08E615.

=== CORRECTIONS ===

Replaced claims: byte 1 of AbilitySceneTable is an ability bit, not an index with a statue nibble; the continue prompt's Yes / No were described the other way round; $06 is the voice sparkle, not the Gaia NPC, and $24 is its voice switch; 'Unmask D-pad and face buttons' ($0F00) is the D-pad only; hpToHeal 40 is a heal request (not 'damage flash ticks'); warpDestX / warpDestY and the $0B08-$0B12 values are the player's spawn position and source scene, not a camera; GaiaNpcSprite loops an idle animation (it is not a single frame); the Shadow flag $B4 is set by Neil, not at Ankor Wat; 'spriteset #05 (transformation frames)' is player body entry #05 and the 'transformation spriteset' of the exit effect is spriteset_enemies; Transform_ShadowToFreedan uses SetEntryHereAndYield, not SetEntryExit.

partNotes.code_list_08DBD4: Continue prompt table: 1 (Yes) = GaiaThenGo ('Then go.'), 2 (No) and 0 (cancel) = GaiaThenRest ('Then rest a while.').
partNotes.LookupAbilityForm: Searches AbilitySceneTable for $0B12 and returns A = 0 when the ability bit is in the low nibble (Will), 1 when it is in the high nibble (Freedan); carry set if the scene is missing (the only caller ignores it). It was first called LookupStatueType after the old 'statue type' reading (there is no statue type).

system/world_map/world_map_options.asm.blockNote:
World map destination menus and their handlers (Bank 03, 242689-244449). WorldMapController runs world_map_options[choice id & $1F] with SwitchCase after SetSavedPtr(DeferSceneTransition); the chosen handler ends in RestoreSavedPtr, which returns to DeferSceneTransition.

=== A MENU (choice ids $01-$1B) ===

PrintDialogString shows a Quit / destination text, then COP DialogueOptions ( grid, skip, &list ) runs MenuSelectionHandler and jumps through the list; the RestoreSavedPtr that follows in the source is never reached (the RTI goes to the list target).
- grid byte: low nibble = items per column, high nibble = total items (0 when everything fits in one column): #01 Quit only, #02 two items, #32 three items, #42 four items. The text puts the second column after the spaces (Quit [N] ... = column one; the text after 8-12 spaces = column two).
- skip byte: text lines skipped before the first option row (#01 everywhere here). The cursor always starts on the first item, Quit.
- list index = MenuSelectionHandler result: 0 = B pressed, 1 = first item (column one, top), 2 = column one, second row, then column two top to bottom. So for #32 / #42 the list order is not the reading order of the text.
- Quit and B both run the same handler: QueueMapChange back to the scene the player came from, with no route (route id stays 0), so DeferSceneTransition dies and the scene changes at once.

=== HANDLERS ===

A trip handler is StageWorldMapMoveIds ( 0, route id ) followed by a QueueMapChange ( scene, X, Y, flags, scroll ) for the destination. Most handlers are two adjacent blocks: the first has no end and falls into the second (the second is also the Quit handler of the destination's own menu). Seven handlers hold both operations in one block. QueueMapChange flag bit 7 ($80) records the destination as the new revive / save point (Inca Ruins, Diamond Mine, Great Wall, Mt.Temple entrance, Angkor Wat, Pyramid). The Watermia to Euro handlers also write $0D60 := 7 (leader animation 7). Menus are named WorldMapMenu_<id> (the choice id in hex; $1C-$25 are WorldMapMenu_Empty<id>, $26 is WorldMapMenu_Nothing26). Handlers are WorldMapGo_<origin>_<destination> (route staging, which falls into the destination's quit block, or both operations in one block) and WorldMapQuit_<place> (QueueMapChange back to that place); WorldMapQuit_Itory_IncaMenu and WorldMapQuit_Watermia_AngelMenu are the second quit blocks of the Itory menu with the Inca Ruins option and of the Angel Village-side Watermia menu.

=== ROUTES (world_map_route_table.asm, Bank 03 241015-242132; the merge tool cannot annotate that file: no bank information) ===

38 table entries ($00-$25) point at 37 route arrays; $00 aliases $01. The arrays are named route_<id>_<origin>_to_<destination> (route_unused_<id> for $0E, $0F, $10, $23, $24 and $25). A step is four bytes: three movement_delta_table indices (X $00CA, Y $00CC, rotation $00BC; 0 = still) and a tick count n. The extraction shows them as route-step < b0, b1, b2, b3 >, which the old header read as flags, direction, spare and distance; that reading is wrong. Every array is 4n + 1 bytes: a hidden $FF ends it; $FE (subroutine) is never used.
Indices used: X and Y take 1 (+1 per tick), 2 (-1), $11 (alternating +1, 0) or $12 (alternating -1, 0); rotation takes 1 (+1) or 2 (-1). Steps never mix rotation with movement: a route turns the map ($20 = 22.5 degrees, $40 = 45, $80 = 90, $C0 = 135) and runs straight in one of eight directions.
Check: summing the steps reproduces the distance between the staged start positions of the two scenes (overworld_exit): route $09 = 128 north, $03 = 16 west and 240 north, $0A = 224 east and 96 south ($0B the reverse), $01 = 48 east and 112 north. These match with n ticks per step; the engine code applies n + 1 deltas, which would add one pixel per axis step (OQ-I060-2).

system/world_map/WorldMapSplitEffect.asm.blockNote:
HDMA thinker of the world-map travel scene (Bank 03, 239678-239936), spawned by WorldMapController's route-launch phase (COP SpawnThinker). Every frame it builds two per-scanline HDMA tables - one for BGMODE ($2105), one for COLDATA ($2132) - that split the screen at a boundary row and, when a route starts, push that row down the screen. The labels of this file were first named after a sine table, a window and an iris (HdmaWindowEffect, QueueHdmaSineBuffers, UpdateHdmaWindowParams, InitSineTableBuffers, loc_ labels, binary_ templates); no sine table or window register is involved. The mnemonics sineTableA, sineTableB and S_sineTableB keep their names because they are shared with the scroll-wave code (ApplyScrollWaveEffect), where they really are sine tables.

=== BUFFERS (double-buffered by frame parity, frameCounter bit 0) ===

Even frames: $7E8800 (BGMODE) and $7E8A00 (COLDATA). Odd frames: $7E8900 (sineTableA) and $7E8B00 (sineTableB). BuildSplitTables rebuilds the pair for the current parity and QueueSplitTables queues exactly that pair with COP QueueDma. The second operand of QueueDma is the PPU B-bus register ($2100 + #05 = BGMODE, #32 = COLDATA; hdma_channel_config gives each register's transfer mode), not an HDMA channel number.

=== TABLE CONTENTS ===

BGMODE (template split_bgmode_template = 7F 07 | 18 07 | 01 09 | 00): 127 lines of $07 (Mode 7), then $18 + offset lines of $07, then one line of $09 (Mode 1 with BG3 priority), then the terminator, which BuildSplitTables writes itself. The last value ($09) stays in force below the table, so the screen is Mode 7 down to row 150 + offset and Mode 1 from row 151 + offset.
COLDATA (template split_coldata_template = 7F 00 | 18 00 | 01 FF | 00): the same line counts with data $00 (no colour plane selected = no change), then one line of $FF (all planes, full intensity = white) on the boundary row. Only the first 6 bytes are copied; the bytes after them are what InitSplitFill left in the buffer: the $01FF fill reads as a count byte $FF (repeat mode, 127 lines) followed by data 01, FF, 01, FF, ..., so every other scanline below the boundary gets a white fixed-colour write. The template's seventh byte is never used.
The per-actor offset in $7F2104,X (0 at spawn) is added to the second line count of both tables, so the boundary row moves by one line per offset step.

=== PHASES (WorldMapSplitEffect) ===

Spawn: offset := 0, InitSplitFill, then SetEntryHere. Every frame the thinker re-enters at the check below that. While worldMapChoiceId ($0D58) is nonzero and worldMapRouteId ($0D5A) is zero (destination chosen, no route playing yet) it only rebuilds and queues the tables with the current offset. Otherwise (no destination, or a route id is set) it runs the opening sequence once: 2 frames of rebuild + queue, then 40 frames in which the offset grows by 2 per frame (second line count $18 -> $68, boundary row 151 -> 231, i.e. off the bottom of the 224-line screen), then it parks on a final SetEntryHere that keeps rebuilding and queuing with offset 80.
What the strip below the boundary looks like on the world map (and whether it is the intended 'iris') is decoded from the tables, not observed (OQ-I058-1).

comments.239718: 40-frame split animation: advance the boundary-row offset by 2 each frame

partNotes.WorldMapControllerEntry: Entry of the controller actor: characterForm := 0, a palette-reset thinker for bundle $0B (twice), ClearAllWramFlags, ArrivalAndTravelSetup spawned as a child (flags $3800), the buttons masked. With no choice id it goes to WorldMapControllerDie; otherwise it yields once, sets the child's animScratch2 bits, saves DeferSceneTransition with SetSavedPtr and runs world_map_options[choice id & $1F].
partNotes.WorldMapControllerDie: The single COP Die shared by the controller (no choice id: a scripted trip, the child does all the work) and by DeferSceneTransition (route id 0: the player chose Quit and the handler already queued the origin scene).
partNotes.SelectFormation: Picks the formation layout for the companions counted by ScanPartyArray: the pointer comes from companion_formation_tables (entry N for N companions) and is kept in $18 / $1A for the dot spawn loop; the leader's animation index (party array word 0) goes to actor $28.
partNotes.FormationDone: All companion dots are spawned: the leader's home pair is its own slot pair (so it dies as soon as the route ends), two AnimOnce frames, the start-area name is cleared, RouteAnimationEngine is spawned before this actor and this actor joins DotAnimationLoop as the leader's dot.
partNotes.DotNextCycle: Animation timer expired: restart the shared dot loop.
partNotes.DotRouteEnded: Route id is 0 (the route is over): the home X is the low byte of orbitDiameter + cameraTargetX; when the dot is already there the Y test follows and the dot dies, otherwise it goes to DotMoveHome.
partNotes.DotMoveHome: Not at home yet: the Y target is the high byte of orbitDiameter ($7F0013) + cameraTargetY, one MoveToward step toward home, then Die.
partNotes.RouteNotEnd: The step byte is not $FF: advance past it; $FE calls a subroutine (RouteSubroutineCall), anything else is the X delta index of a normal step.
partNotes.RouteDeltaTables: Normal step: the X, Y and rotation delta chains are looked up in movement_delta_table ($18, $1A, $1C) and the tick count n is stored in $24; SetEntryHere then yields one frame per tick.
partNotes.RouteAxisY: X axis done or absent (null chain pointer): handle the Y axis in the same way (chain pointer $1A, world Y $00CC, cameraTargetY = Y - $70).
partNotes.RouteAxisRotation: Y axis done or absent: add the rotation delta chain $1C to the rotation index $BC.
partNotes.RouteCountTick: End of the tick: decrement the remaining tick count; while it is still non-negative the actor yields (RTL).
partNotes.RouteNextStep: The count went negative: the step is complete, continue with the next one at RouteStepLoop.
partNotes.ClearStateLoop: Zero-fill loop of ClearWorldMapState: 14 words from $0D52 to $0D6D.
partNotes.LookupMapNameLoop: Search loop of LookupMapName: compare the scene id of entry X with $0000; a zero id byte ends the search (miss), a match goes to LookupMapNameFound, otherwise X advances by 3.
partNotes.LookupMapNameFound: Match: Y := the name pointer at world_map_scene_names + 1 + X, restore DBR / X / P and return.
partNotes.LookupMapNameMiss: Zero id byte reached (no match, OQ-I059-7): restore DBR / X / P and return with Y unchanged.

partNotes.palette_bundle_enix_obj1_settle: Bundle $55: the same frames as $54 on OBJ palette 1. Stage 3 of boot_logo_enix_palette_obj1.
partNotes.palette_bundle_enix_obj2_fill_a: Bundle $56: 8 frames on OBJ palette 2 (CGRAM $A1-$AF); starts black and fills the 15 colours with the flat purple $68DA one at a time (colours 1-8). Stage 1 of boot_logo_enix_palette_obj2.
partNotes.palette_bundle_enix_obj2_fill_b: Bundle $57: continues the purple fill from 9 colours to all 15 (the last two frames are both full). Stage 2 of boot_logo_enix_palette_obj2.
partNotes.palette_bundle_enix_obj2_dip: Bundle $58: starts all purple; a darker dip opens around colour 7 and widens each frame, ending in a V-shaped ramp that is held for 34 ticks. Stage 3 of boot_logo_enix_palette_obj2.
